title: Grains, Anchors, Composite Type, Solved Springs & the Skinned Player
description: Five patterns that hand the work to a rule: a sampled view, a 1995 layout pass, per-script font tuning, a spring solved on paper, and custom elements.

drops.title: Views That Turn to Grains
drops.description: An exit that doesn't move the view — it ends it, by sampling the whole thing once into a few hundred coloured quads.
drops.concept: The view is captured into a grid of grains and from then on only the grains are animated, each by one pure step function over its own local time. Six presets — sand, ember, pixel, vortex, shatter, melt — share the engine, and because the step takes a normalised t, playing it backwards reassembles the card. The cascade is a per-grain delay taken from its distance to the point you touched.
drops.source: rs-4/dissolve — Skia makeImageFromView + Reanimated 4 atlas, 8 presets, capped at 6000 grains per burst

interaction.mouse: The point you press becomes the origin the cascade radiates from.
interaction.click: Tap a card to dissolve it; tap again to run the same curve backwards.
interaction.touch: Pointer events throughout — tap anywhere on a card.

drops.title: Anchored, Docked, Flowed
drops.description: Three resizable windows whose children are placed by a layout pass in code — anchors, docking and flow — not by a stylesheet.
drops.concept: Before CSS had an opinion, resizable forms solved layout with three rules. Docked controls are carved out of the client rectangle in declaration order, each shrinking what remains; anchored controls take a share of the delta on every edge they are tied to, stretching when tied to both; a flow panel just walks the leftovers and wraps. Drag any hatched corner and watch the rule decide what moves.
drops.source: wieslawsoltes/VB6 — VB6 Studio Web, whose @vb6/auto-layout adds Windows-Forms edge anchoring, docking and flow to the classic form designer

interaction.mouse: Drag a window's bottom-right grip to resize it; click any control to select it.
interaction.click: Toggle anchors or pick a dock side in the panel and the layout pass re-runs.
interaction.touch: The grips and controls are pointer-driven, so dragging works on touch.

drops.title: One Font Per Script
drops.description: A @font-face per character class, each with its own face and its own size-adjust, so digits and kana stop fighting the text face.
drops.concept: A plain font stack already routes each character to a face that can draw it — what it never does is balance them. Give each class its own @font-face with a unicode-range and a size-adjust and the browser rescales just that face in place. Every specimen shows the plain stack above and the balanced composite below; the generated CSS is printed live underneath.
drops.source: charlie5188/css-composite-font — Composite Font Studio, InDesign-style per-class composition for CJK and Western text, tuned per weight

interaction.mouse: Drag the per-class sliders and every specimen re-renders from regenerated @font-face rules.
interaction.click: Toggle the baseline control to see what a real composite font bakes into its outlines.
interaction.touch: Sliders are native range inputs; the panel moves inline on narrow screens.

drops.title: Outlines on Springs
drops.description: One contour re-sampled so both shapes share their points, with a closed-form damped spring carrying every point across.
drops.concept: Not a cross-fade between icons: each shape is a radius function sampled at the same 128 angles, so point i of the circle and point i of the star are the same point in two poses and morphing is a per-point lerp. The spring is solved analytically rather than integrated, so there is no accumulation and no drift — ask for the value at t and get it, velocity included when you interrupt it mid-flight.
drops.source: useFluid/fluidui — Metamorph contour morphing between any two shapes, driven by closed-form springs with no dependencies

interaction.mouse: Hover the dock icons to morph their outlines; press and hold a button to squash it.
interaction.click: Tap the big shape to advance to the next contour in the cycle.
interaction.touch: Tapping an icon toggles its morph; the stiffness, damping and mass sliders retune every spring at once.

drops.title: The Player, as Elements
drops.description: A window that drags and resizes itself, an LCD that is also a scrub control, ten EQ bands that really shape the spectrum.
drops.concept: The skinned media player was the original component library, and it maps cleanly onto custom elements: sk-window writes its own --x/--y/--w while you drag, sk-slider turns a pointer into a value and an input event, sk-lcd is a readout, a marquee, a spectrum and a seek control at once. All light DOM, four element definitions, no framework runtime.
drops.source: rauchg/winamp-ui-sdk — Winamp 5 Modern recreated in pure Web Components on @ui-sdk/web, light DOM, resize streaming CSS variables

interaction.mouse: Drag titlebars to move windows and the hatched corner to resize; drag across the LCD to scrub.
interaction.click: Transport buttons, EQ toggles, FLAT/SMILE presets, playlist rows and four skins all respond.
interaction.touch: Every control is pointer-based with touch-action none, so dragging sliders works on a phone.
